{{Quote|All that life extinguished&hellip; It's unthinkable.|General [[Var Suthra]]|<ref name="Uphrades" />}}
In [[3643 BBY]], during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Angral]] '''devastated''' the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Uphrades]] using the [[Desolator (superweapon)|Desolator]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]]. The penultimate event of his [[Desolator crisis|campaign]] of vengeance against the Republic and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] for the [[Death/Legends|death]] of his son, [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]], Angral's attack on the [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] of Uphrades was a way to test his newly-constructed weapon before using it to [[Battle of the Oppressor|attack]] [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. The Desolator weapon ravaged Uphrades' surface and [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], killing millions of civilians, and before departing for the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]], Angral dispatched a boarding team to destroy the [[Hospital ship/Legends|medical frigate]] ''[[Daybreaker]]'' in order to eliminate any witnesses.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|We've just picked up the tracking beacon's signal in the Uphrades system. That agriworld supplies nearly half of Coruscant's food. I'm scrambling the fleet, but you're closer.|General Var Suthra|<ref name="Uphrades" />}}
In [[3643 BBY]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]] was [[Death/Legends|killed]] in a [[Duel in the Jedi Temple ruins|duel]] with a [[Hero of Tython|young Jedi Knight]] during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]]. Tarnis, who had been working undercover as a [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] on the [[Republic superweapon initiative]],<ref name="Race to the Ruins">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Race to the Ruins|Coruscant}}</ref> had used his access to the Republic's [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] projects to develop a method of combining the [[Death Mark laser]], [[Shock Drum]], and [[Planet Prison]] weapons into a single [[Starship/Legends|ship]]-mounted weapon capable of destroying a [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. Tarnis named the weapon the [[Desolator (superweapon)|Desolator]], and he sent his [[Parent/Legends|father]], [[Darth Angral]], copies of the design files<ref name="New Intelligence">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|New Intelligence|Ord Mantell}}</ref> during his [[Mission to Coruscant (Desolator crisis)|attempt]] to use the Planet Prison against the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Tarnis's plans were foiled when the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] killed him in battle, causing Angral to embark on a [[Desolator crisis|campaign of vengeance]] against the Republic and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in response, and Angral dispatched his three [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentices]] to capture the Republic's offworld weapon facilities across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Race to the Ruins" />

With Tarnis's design files, Angral constructed the Desolator weapon and installed it on his personal [[Harrower-class dreadnought|''Harrower''-class dreadnought]], the [[Oppressor (Harrower-class)|''Oppressor'']].<ref name="New Intelligence" /> The [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Orgus Din]]&mdash;a personal enemy of Angral and the former Master of the Knight who had killed Tarnis&mdash;[[Mission to the Oppressor|attempted]] to sneak aboard the [[Warship/Legends|warship]] in the [[Alderaan system/Legends|Alderaan system]] and kill Angral, but he was only able to install a [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking device]] before the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] captured and executed him. Angral then departed the [[Star system/Legends|star system]], jettisoning Din's body into [[Realspace/Legends|space]],<ref name="Facing Lord Nefarid" /> and traveled to the [[Uphrades system/Legends|Uphrades system]] to test the completed Desolator weapon on the Republic [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] of [[Uphrades]].<ref name="Uphrades" />

==The devastation==
{{Quote|When we arrived, an Imperial warship was attacking the planet. I've never seen anything like it.''"<br />"''Uphrades was trapped inside an energy field. Some starships tried to flee, but their engines failed before they could leave the atmosphere.''"<br />"''No one escaped. Every ship that tried crashed back onto the surface.|Doctor Senessa and Captain Dal|<ref name="Uphrades" />}}
Upon entering the Uphrades system, the ''Oppressor'' fired the Desolator at the planet, [[Ion cannon/Legends|ionizing]] Uphrades' [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] and trapping all starships on the surface. The Desolator was wreaking havoc on the planet through seismic vibrations when the Republic [[Hospital ship/Legends|medical frigate]] ''[[Daybreaker]]'' arrived in the system, and the ship's crew watched as the final stages of the Desolator set Uphrades' atmosphere on [[Fire/Legends|fire]], and the planet tore itself apart. The attack on Uphrades wiped out the planet's 16 million inhabitants, leaving only a few hundred survivors scattered across the ruined surface of the world. Upon sighting the ''Daybreaker'', the ''Oppressor'' dispatched boarding pods to capture the vessel and eliminate all witnesses. Satisfied that the weapon was operational, Angral ordered the ''Oppressor'' to depart for [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Order.<ref name="Uphrades" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Our sensors detect faint life readings on the planet's surface&mdash;possible survivors.''"<br />"''Anyone left on that planet is as good as dead.''"<br />"''If we go down there, we can provide food, water, shelter and medicine. It's our duty.|Doctor Senessa and Captain Dal|<ref name="Uphrades" />}}
Not long after Angral's departure, the Jedi Knight responsible for Tarnis's death arrived in the Uphrades system, having followed the signal from Orgus Din's tracking device. Along with the Jedi's [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Kira Carsen]], and the [[T7-series astromech droid|astromech droid]] [[T7-O1]], the Knight foiled the Imperial [[Attack on the Daybreaker|attack]] on the ''Daybreaker'' and rescued the ship's crew. The ''Daybreaker''{{'s}} [[chief medical officer]], [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Senessa]], detected scattered life signs on Uphrades' surface amid the widespread destruction, and she proposed that the ''Daybreaker'' land on the planet to give them aid even though the atmosphere would disable the ship.<ref name="Uphrades" />

{{GameLS|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
Despite the attempts of [[Dal (Cathar)|Dal]], the ''Daybreaker''{{'s}} [[Captain/Legends|captain]], to bribe the Knight, the Jedi agreed with Senessa's proposal, and she took command of the vessel in order to aid the survivors. With the help of the ''Daybreaker''{{'s}} crew, the survivors endured on Uphrades' surface during the [[Standard month/Legends|months]] that it took for the ionization of the planet's atmosphere to fade and allow rescue attempts.<ref name="Uphrades" />
{{Endgame}}

Upon learning of Angral's intent to target Tython, the Jedi and crew pursued the ''Oppressor'' to the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] and boarded the vessel while the Desolator was undergoing the lengthy charging process necessary to fire. With the ''Daybreaker''{{'s}} scans of the ''Oppressor'', the Republic scientist Doctor [[Nasan Godera]] located a flaw in the Desolator's power systems that allowed the Knight and Carsen to disable the superweapon by deactivating the ''Oppressor''{{'s}} [[Reactor/Legends|reactors]]. When the two Jedi confronted Angral aboard the ''Oppressor''{{'s}} [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], the Sith Lord revealed that he had attacked Uphrades to lure his son's killer into a final confrontation&mdash;but their battle ended with Angral's death and the destruction of both the ''Oppressor'' and the Desolator, ensuring that no other planet would suffer the fate of Uphrades.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Fate of the Jedi|the ''Oppressor''}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The superweapon attack on Uphrades first appeared in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released by [[BioWare]] and [[LucasArts]] in [[2011]], during the Jedi Knight-class mission "Uphrades." Captain Dal presents a dialogue option in which players can convince Doctor Senessa to abandon the survivors, a choice that rewards the player with medical supplies, or choose to ignore his request and allow Senessa to take the ''Daybreaker'' down to Uphrades.<ref name="Uphrades" /> This article assumes that the player chooses only the moral [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] options as a Republic Jedi Knight character,<ref name="Light Side">This article assumes that the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] classes in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' choose the options that provide the most [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] alignment points.</ref> and it therefore assumes that Senessa takes command of the ''Daybreaker''.<ref name="Uphrades" />
